subproblems.title: Hilbert–Schmidt identity Σ_j α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|² for every orthonormal basis f (parent (L0); reused accepted DAG theorem)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) n, a continuous alternating n-linear form on ℝ^P = Euclid P) and let f = (f_0, …, f_{P−1}) be an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P. Then Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f_{j(0)}, …, f_{j(n−1)})² = n!·|α|², where |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} and e is the standard basis of ℝ^P. This is identity (L0) of the parent proof. It is exactly the comparator-accepted DAG theorem regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis, reused with its identical frozen Lean type.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Euclid P)), ∑ j : Fin n → Fin P, (α (fun k => f (j k))) ^ 2 = (n.factorial : ℝ) * covectorEuclideanNorm α ^ 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused accepted theorem. This is identity (L0) of the selected parent proof (steps 1–2 there), and it is exactly the comparator-accepted DAG theorem regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis (node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.imrep_mass_formula-a1.covector_sq_sum-a1, status accepted, candidate 16144a475b), reused with its byte-identical frozen Lean type. The proof below is the one accepted for that node, copied verbatim.

Source: steps 1(i)–(ii) of the parent node's supplied proof of the mass formula M_W(T) = R.measure W (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3), chapter-06.txt lines 763–766; coefficient norm of (6.1.5)/(6.1.15)). Notation (shared with the parent proof): ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with standard orthonormal basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i; Λ^n = Covector (Euclid P) n, the continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P; for a family b : Fin P → ℝ^P and j : Fin n → Fin P write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(n−1)}); |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} [I strictly increasing] α(e∘I)²) (SimonGMT Chapter06/Mass.lean). For a family b put S_b(α) := Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(b∘j)². We must show S_f(α) = n!·|α|_E².

1. (Square of the norm.) The radicand Σ_I [I strictly increasing] α(e∘I)² is a finite sum of nonnegative terms, so |α|_E² = Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e∘I)² (Real.sq_sqrt).

2. (Basis independence by slotwise Parseval.) Let b, b' be orthonormal bases of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P. For m = 0, 1, …, n put H_m := Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(w_m(j))², where w_m(j)(k) := b_{j(k)} if k < m and w_m(j)(k) := b'_{j(k)} if k ≥ m. Then H_0 = S_{b'}(α) and H_n = S_b(α). Fix m < n and split every j into its m-th value i := j(m) ∈ Fin P and its values j' on the other n − 1 slots (j ↦ (j(m), j') is a bijection, e.g. via Fin.insertNth / Fin.removeNth). For fixed j' the map λ_{j'}(v) := α(u_0, …, u_{m−1}, v, u_{m+1}, …, u_{n−1}), with u_k := b_{j(k)} for k < m and u_k := b'_{j(k)} for k > m, is a linear functional of v ∈ ℝ^P (α is multilinear). Writing λ_{j'}(v) = ⟨r, v⟩ with r := Σ_a λ_{j'}(e_a) e_a, Parseval for orthonormal bases (OrthonormalBasis.sum_sq_inner_right) gives Σ_i λ_{j'}(b_i)² = ‖r‖² = Σ_i λ_{j'}(b'_i)². The terms of H_{m+1} with fixed j' are exactly the λ_{j'}(b_i)² (i ∈ Fin P) and those of H_m are the λ_{j'}(b'_i)²; summing over j' gives H_{m+1} = H_m. By induction on m, S_b(α) = S_{b'}(α); in particular S_f(α) = S_e(α). (Equivalent implementation: expand b_i = Σ_a ⟨e_a, b_i⟩ e_a in every slot by multilinearity and use Σ_i ⟨e_a, b_i⟩⟨e_{a'}, b_i⟩ = δ_{aa'} (OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner) in each of the n slots; all cross terms cancel and S_b(α) = S_e(α).)

3. (Non-injective tuples.) If j is not injective then e∘j is not injective (e is injective), so α(e∘j) = 0 because α is alternating (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_not_injective). Hence S_e(α) = Σ_{j injective} α(e∘j)².

4. (Injective tuples = increasing tuples × permutations.) Every injective j : Fin n → Fin P factors uniquely as j = I∘π with I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing and π ∈ Perm(Fin n). Existence: with σ := Tuple.sort j, j∘σ is monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort) and injective, hence strictly increasing; take I := j∘σ and π := σ⁻¹. Uniqueness: if I∘π = I'∘π' with I, I' strictly increasing, then I and I' have the same range, and a strictly increasing map Fin n → Fin P is determined by its range (it is the increasing enumeration of that n-element set, cf. StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT / Finset.orderEmbOfFin_unique), so I = I'; then π = π' because I is injective. Conversely each such I∘π is injective. Thus (I, π) ↦ I∘π is a bijection from {I strictly increasing} × Perm(Fin n) onto {j injective}.

5. (Signs.) For I strictly increasing and π ∈ Perm(Fin n), α(e∘I∘π) = sign(π)·α(e∘I) (AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to α.toAlternatingMap), so α(e∘(I∘π))² = α(e∘I)².

6. (Counting.) By steps 3–5, S_e(α) = Σ_{I strictly increasing} Σ_{π ∈ Perm(Fin n)} α(e∘I)² = |Perm(Fin n)|·Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e∘I)² = n!·|α|_E² (Fintype.card_perm, Fintype.card_fin and step 1).

7. (Conclusion.) By steps 2 and 6, Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = S_f(α) = S_e(α) = n!·|α|_E². The same argument covers n = 0 (one empty tuple, which is strictly increasing; 0! = 1) and n > P (no injective and no strictly increasing tuples; both sides are 0). ∎
proof_key_steps: |α|_E² equals the sum of α(e∘I)² over strictly increasing I.
Slotwise Parseval (hybrid sums H_m) shows Σ_j α(b∘j)² is the same for every orthonormal basis b.
Non-injective tuples contribute 0; injective tuples are exactly I∘π (I increasing, π a permutation) and contribute α(e∘I)² each.
Counting the n! permutations gives Σ_j α(e∘j)² = n!·|α|_E², hence Σ_j α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|_E².

subproblems.title: Evaluation on an orthonormal frame is bounded by the coefficient norm: |α(τ)| ≤ |α| (parent (L3); reused accepted DAG theorem)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) n) and let τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P = Euclid P. Then |α(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1})| ≤ |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α. This is conjunct (L3) of the parent statement with N := P and k := n. It is exactly the comparator-accepted DAG theorem regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le, reused with its identical frozen Lean type.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → |α τ| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused accepted theorem. This is conjunct (L3) of the selected parent statement (step 3 of the parent proof), written with the bound variables P := N, n := k. It is exactly the comparator-accepted DAG theorem regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le (node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.imrep_mass_formula-a1.covector_eval_le-a1, status accepted, candidate b7846b6399), reused with its byte-identical frozen Lean type. Its proof uses the sibling sq_sum (regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis). The proof below is the one accepted for that node, copied verbatim.

Source: step 1(a) of the parent node's supplied proof of the mass formula M_W(T) = R.measure W (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3)). Notation (shared with the parent proof): ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with standard orthonormal basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i; Λ^n = Covector (Euclid P) n, the continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P; for a family b : Fin P → ℝ^P and j : Fin n → Fin P write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(n−1)}); |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} [I strictly increasing] α(e∘I)²) (SimonGMT Chapter06/Mass.lean). Uses the sibling lemma regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis: for every orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P, Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|_E².

1. (n ≤ P and an orthonormal basis extending τ.) τ is orthonormal, hence linearly independent, so n = card(Fin n) ≤ finrank ℝ ℝ^P = P (Orthonormal.linearIndependent, LinearIndependent.fintype_card_le_finrank, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). Let ι : Fin n → Fin P, ι(k) := Fin.castLE (n ≤ P) k (injective). Define v : Fin P → ℝ^P by v(i) := τ(⟨i, h⟩) if h : i.val < n and v(i) := 0 otherwise, and s := {i : Fin P | i.val < n}. The restriction of v to s is τ composed with the bijection s ≃ Fin n, hence orthonormal. Since finrank ℝ ℝ^P = P = card(Fin P), Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq gives an orthonormal basis f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ ℝ^P with f(i) = v(i) for all i ∈ s; in particular f(ι(k)) = τ(k) for every k ∈ Fin n.

2. (Permuted frames.) For π ∈ Perm(Fin n) we have τ∘π = f∘(ι∘π), and α(τ∘π) = sign(π)·α(τ) (AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to α.toAlternatingMap), so α(f∘(ι∘π))² = α(τ)².

3. (Comparison with the full sum.) The map π ↦ ι∘π from Perm(Fin n) to Fin n → Fin P is injective (ι is injective), and every term α(f∘j)² is ≥ 0. Hence n!·α(τ)² = Σ_{π ∈ Perm(Fin n)} α(f∘(ι∘π))² ≤ Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f∘j)² (the left sum is a sum over the image of an injective map: Finset.sum_image, Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg; |Perm(Fin n)| = n! by Fintype.card_perm, Fintype.card_fin).

4. (Sibling identity.) By regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis applied to P, n, α, f, the right-hand side equals n!·|α|_E². Dividing by n! > 0 gives α(τ)² ≤ |α|_E².

5. (Conclusion.) Since |α|_E ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg), α(τ)² ≤ |α|_E² implies |α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E (abs_le_of_sq_le_sq' / sq_le_sq'). ∎
proof_key_steps: n ≤ P and τ extends to an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P (indexed by Fin P) with f(castLE k) = τ(k).
The sibling identity gives Σ_j α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|_E², hence |α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E.

subproblems.title: Pull-back bound for the coefficient norm: |A^#β| ≤ ‖A‖^k·|β| (parent (L1))
subproblems.statement: Let N, N', k ∈ ℕ, let A : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} be a continuous linear map (A : Euclid N →L[ℝ] Euclid N') with operator norm ‖A‖, and let β be a k-covector on ℝ^{N'} (Covector (Euclid N') k). Let A^#β := β.compContinuousLinearMap A be the pull-back, A^#β(w_1, …, w_k) = β(Aw_1, …, Aw_k). Then |A^#β| ≤ ‖A‖^k·|β|, where |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α is the Euclidean norm of the values of α on the strictly increasing tuples of standard basis vectors of the respective space.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N N' k : ℕ) (A : Euclid N →L[ℝ] Euclid N') (β : Covector (Euclid N') k), covectorEuclideanNorm (β.compContinuousLinearMap A) ≤ ‖A‖ ^ k * covectorEuclideanNorm β
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4–5 of the selected parent proof (the one-slot estimate T_j ≤ ‖A‖²·T_{j−1}, iterated over the k slots, then (L0)). The telescoping over the slots is written here as an induction on the degree that peels off the first slot with ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft. Each induction step applies the parent's one-slot estimate to one slot. Uses the sibling sq_sum (regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis).

Notation. ℝ^M = Euclid M = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin M). e = (e_a)_{a ∈ Fin N} := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin N) ℝ is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^N, and e' = (e'_b)_{b ∈ Fin N'} that of ℝ^{N'}. For an m-covector γ on ℝ^M, an orthonormal basis b of ℝ^M indexed by Fin M and j : Fin m → Fin M, write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(m−1)}) and S_b(γ) := Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin M} γ(b∘j)². |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. For x ∈ ℝ^M and an (m+1)-covector γ, ι_xγ := γ.curryLeft x is the m-covector w ↦ γ(x, w_0, …, w_{m−1}) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply: γ.curryLeft x w = γ (Matrix.vecCons x w), and Matrix.vecCons x w = Fin.cons x w). The map x ↦ ι_xγ is continuous linear. For an m-covector γ on ℝ^{N'}, A^#γ := γ.compContinuousLinearMap A, so (A^#γ)(w) = γ(Aw_0, …, Aw_{m−1}) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply).

1. (Parseval for functionals.) Let M ∈ ℕ, let e^{(M)}_a := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin M) ℝ a (a ∈ Fin M) be the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^M, and let μ : ℝ^M → ℝ be continuous linear. Then Σ_{a ∈ Fin M} μ(e^{(M)}_a)² = ‖μ‖². Proof: by the Riesz representation (InnerProductSpace.toDual, a linear isometric equivalence) there is g := (toDual ℝ ℝ^M)⁻¹(μ) with μ(x) = ⟨g, x⟩ for every x (InnerProductSpace.toDual_symm_apply) and ‖g‖ = ‖μ‖. Parseval for the orthonormal basis e^{(M)} (OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner) gives Σ_a ⟨g, e^{(M)}_a⟩·⟨e^{(M)}_a, g⟩ = ⟨g, g⟩ = ‖g‖². Hence Σ_a μ(e^{(M)}_a)² = Σ_a ⟨g, e^{(M)}_a⟩² = ‖g‖² = ‖μ‖². (For M = N, e^{(N)} = e; for M = N', e^{(N')} = e'.)

2. (One-slot estimate.) For every continuous linear functional μ : ℝ^{N'} → ℝ, Σ_{a ∈ Fin N} μ(Ae_a)² ≤ ‖A‖²·Σ_{b ∈ Fin N'} μ(e'_b)². Proof: μ∘A is a continuous linear functional on ℝ^N. By step 1 with M = N (basis e) the left side equals ‖μ∘A‖². By step 1 with M = N' (basis e') the right side equals ‖A‖²·‖μ‖². Since 0 ≤ ‖μ∘A‖ ≤ ‖μ‖·‖A‖ (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_comp_le), squaring gives ‖μ∘A‖² ≤ ‖A‖²·‖μ‖². (This is the parent's estimate Σ_i ⟨g, Ae_i⟩² = |A*g|² ≤ ‖A‖²·|g|², since A*g is the Riesz vector of μ∘A.)

3. (First-slot reindexing.) For M, m ∈ ℕ and every F : (Fin (m+1) → Fin M) → ℝ, Σ_{J : Fin (m+1) → Fin M} F(J) = Σ_{a ∈ Fin M} Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin M} F(Fin.cons a j). The reason is that (a, j) ↦ Fin.cons a j is a bijection Fin M × (Fin m → Fin M) → (Fin (m+1) → Fin M) (Fin.consEquiv; Fintype.sum_prod_type). Moreover, for every family b, b∘(Fin.cons a j) = Fin.cons b_a (b∘j) (Fin.comp_cons; check on slot 0 and on the slots i+1). Hence γ(b∘Fin.cons a j) = (ι_{b_a}γ)(b∘j) for every (m+1)-covector γ.

4. (Hilbert–Schmidt inequality.) Claim H(m), for every m ∈ ℕ: every m-covector γ on ℝ^{N'} satisfies S_e(A^#γ) ≤ (‖A‖²)^m·S_{e'}(γ). Proof by induction on m.
(a) m = 0. Each of Fin 0 → Fin N and Fin 0 → Fin N' has exactly one element, the empty tuple. All tuples Fin 0 → ℝ^{N'} are equal. So both sums consist of the single term γ(∅)², hence S_e(A^#γ) = S_{e'}(γ) = (‖A‖²)^0·S_{e'}(γ).
(b) Step m → m+1. Let γ be an (m+1)-covector on ℝ^{N'}. For x ∈ ℝ^N, ι_x(A^#γ) = A^#(ι_{Ax}γ), because both send w to γ(Ax, Aw_0, …, Aw_{m−1}) (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_compContinuousLinearMap). By step 3 for e,
S_e(A^#γ) = Σ_{a ∈ Fin N} Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin N} (A^#(ι_{Ae_a}γ))(e∘j)² = Σ_a S_e(A^#(ι_{Ae_a}γ)).
By H(m) for the m-covector ι_{Ae_a}γ, and then exchanging the two finite sums, this is
≤ Σ_a (‖A‖²)^m·S_{e'}(ι_{Ae_a}γ) = (‖A‖²)^m·Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin N'} Σ_{a ∈ Fin N} (ι_{Ae_a}γ)(e'∘j)².
Fix j. μ_j(u) := (ι_uγ)(e'∘j) = γ(u, e'_{j(0)}, …, e'_{j(m−1)}) is a continuous linear functional of u ∈ ℝ^{N'}: it is u ↦ ι_uγ composed with evaluation at e'∘j (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply). By step 2, Σ_a μ_j(Ae_a)² ≤ ‖A‖²·Σ_{b ∈ Fin N'} μ_j(e'_b)². Multiply by (‖A‖²)^m ≥ 0, sum over j, exchange the sums and use step 3 for e':
S_e(A^#γ) ≤ (‖A‖²)^{m+1}·Σ_{b ∈ Fin N'} Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin N'} γ(e'∘Fin.cons b j)² = (‖A‖²)^{m+1}·S_{e'}(γ).
This proves H(m+1). (Each application of step 2 replaces the vectors Ae_a in one slot by the basis vectors e'_b. This is the parent's chain T_k ≤ ‖A‖²·T_{k−1} ≤ … ≤ ‖A‖^{2k}·T_0, organized as an induction.)

5. (Factorial identity, (L0).) By the sibling sq_sum (regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis), applied to the k-covector A^#β with the orthonormal basis e of ℝ^N and to β with the orthonormal basis e' of ℝ^{N'}: S_e(A^#β) = k!·|A^#β|² and S_{e'}(β) = k!·|β|².

6. (Conclusion.) H(k) for γ = β together with step 5 gives k!·|A^#β|² ≤ (‖A‖²)^k·k!·|β|² = k!·(‖A‖^k·|β|)². Since k! > 0, |A^#β|² ≤ (‖A‖^k·|β|)². Both |A^#β| and ‖A‖^k·|β| are ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg, norm_nonneg), so |A^#β| ≤ ‖A‖^k·|β| (pow_le_pow_iff_left₀ with exponent 2). That is, covectorEuclideanNorm (β.compContinuousLinearMap A) ≤ ‖A‖ ^ k * covectorEuclideanNorm β. For k = 0 the argument gives |A^#β| ≤ 1·|β| (both equal |β(∅)|, the value on the empty tuple). ∎
proof_key_steps: Parseval for functionals: Σ_a μ(e_a)² = ‖μ‖² (Riesz representation and OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner); hence the one-slot estimate Σ_a μ(Ae_a)² ≤ ‖A‖²·Σ_b μ(e'_b)² via ‖μ∘A‖ ≤ ‖μ‖‖A‖.
First-slot reindexing J = Fin.cons a j and ι_x(A^#γ) = A^#(ι_{Ax}γ) (curryLeft_compContinuousLinearMap).
Hilbert–Schmidt inequality S_e(A^#γ) ≤ (‖A‖²)^m·S_{e'}(γ) by induction on the degree m: induction hypothesis on ι_{Ae_a}γ, then the one-slot estimate on the first slot.
sq_sum turns both sums into k!·|·|²; cancel k! and take square roots of nonnegative quantities.

subproblems.title: Interior-product bound for the coefficient norm: |ι_vβ| ≤ |v|·|β| (parent (L2))
subproblems.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ, let v ∈ ℝ^N = Euclid N and let β be a (k+1)-covector on ℝ^N (Covector (Euclid N) (k+1)). Let ι_vβ := β.curryLeft v be the interior product, the k-covector ι_vβ(w_1, …, w_k) = β(v, w_1, …, w_k). Then |ι_vβ| ≤ ‖v‖·|β|, where ‖v‖ is the Euclidean norm of v and |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α is the Euclidean norm of the values of α on the strictly increasing tuples of standard basis vectors.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (v : Euclid N) (β : Covector (Euclid N) (k + 1)), covectorEuclideanNorm (β.curryLeft v) ≤ ‖v‖ * covectorEuclideanNorm β
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the selected parent proof. That step rotates v to a basis vector f_{i₀}. It compares the Hilbert–Schmidt sums of ι_{f_{i₀}}β and β by the position at which the index i₀ occurs. The parent keeps only the tuples in which i₀ occurs exactly once. Here that count is written with the position sums R_p below. Uses the sibling sq_sum (regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis).

Notation. ℝ^N = Euclid N with standard basis e. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{J strictly increasing} α(e∘J)²)^{1/2}. For an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^N indexed by Fin N and J : Fin m → Fin N, write f∘J := (f_{J(0)}, …, f_{J(m−1)}). For x ∈ ℝ^N, ι_xβ := β.curryLeft x is the k-covector w ↦ β(x, w_0, …, w_{k−1}) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply: β.curryLeft x w = β (Matrix.vecCons x w), and Matrix.vecCons x w = Fin.cons x w). β.curryLeft is a continuous linear map in x, so ι_{cx}β = c·ι_xβ and ι_0β = 0.

1. (Homogeneity of the coefficient norm.) For c ∈ ℝ and a k-covector γ: |c·γ| = |c|·|γ|. Each coefficient satisfies (c·γ)(e∘J) = c·γ(e∘J), so the radicand of |c·γ| is c² times the radicand X ≥ 0 of |γ|. Then √(c²·X) = √(c²)·√X = |c|·√X (Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).

2. (Case v = 0.) Then ι_vβ = 0, so |ι_vβ| = 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero), and the right side ‖0‖·|β| = 0. Assume from now on v ≠ 0. Then N ≥ 1, since ℝ^0 = {0}. Put i₀ := 0 ∈ Fin N.

3. (Rotating v to a basis vector.) Put u := ‖v‖⁻¹·v. Then ‖u‖ = 1 and v = ‖v‖·u. The one-member family (u) indexed by the set {i₀} is orthonormal (a single unit vector), and finrank ℝ^N = N = card (Fin N). So Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq gives an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^N indexed by Fin N with f_{i₀} = u. By linearity, ι_vβ = ‖v‖·ι_uβ. By step 1 and ‖v‖ ≥ 0, |ι_vβ| = ‖v‖·|ι_uβ|. It therefore suffices to show |ι_uβ| ≤ |β|.

4. (Position sums.) For J : Fin (k+1) → Fin N put g(J) := β(f∘J)² ≥ 0. For each position p ∈ Fin (k+1) put R_p := Σ_{J : Fin (k+1) → Fin N} [J(p) = i₀]·g(J), where [·] is 1 if the condition holds and 0 otherwise.

5. (R_0 = k!·|ι_uβ|².) (a, j) ↦ Fin.cons a j is a bijection Fin N × (Fin k → Fin N) → (Fin (k+1) → Fin N) (Fin.consEquiv). Under it the condition J(0) = i₀ becomes a = i₀, so R_0 = Σ_{j : Fin k → Fin N} β(f∘Fin.cons i₀ j)². Since f∘Fin.cons i₀ j = Fin.cons f_{i₀} (f∘j) = Fin.cons u (f∘j) (Fin.comp_cons), each term equals (ι_uβ)(f∘j)². Hence R_0 = Σ_{j : Fin k → Fin N} (ι_uβ)(f∘j)² = k!·|ι_uβ|², by sq_sum applied to the k-covector ι_uβ and the orthonormal basis f.

6. (R_p = R_0 for every p.) Let σ := Equiv.swap 0 p, the transposition of 0 and p in Fin (k+1) (σ is the identity if p = 0). Then σ⁻¹ = σ and σ⁻¹(0) = p. The map J ↦ J∘σ⁻¹ is a bijection of Fin (k+1) → Fin N (Equiv.arrowCongr σ (Equiv.refl _)). We have (J∘σ⁻¹)(0) = J(p). Also β(f∘J∘σ⁻¹) = sign(σ⁻¹)·β(f∘J) (AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to β.toAlternatingMap), and sign(σ⁻¹) = ±1, so g(J∘σ⁻¹) = g(J). Substituting J ↦ J∘σ⁻¹ in R_0 gives R_0 = Σ_J [(J∘σ⁻¹)(0) = i₀]·g(J∘σ⁻¹) = Σ_J [J(p) = i₀]·g(J) = R_p. (This is the parent's remark that moving f_{i₀} to the front only permutes the arguments, so β(f_{I'}) = ±β(f_{i₀}, f_I).)

7. (Σ_p R_p ≤ Σ_J g(J).) Exchanging the finite sums gives Σ_{p ∈ Fin (k+1)} R_p = Σ_J c(J)·g(J), where c(J) := #{p ∈ Fin (k+1) : J(p) = i₀}. If c(J) ≤ 1, then c(J)·g(J) ≤ g(J) because g(J) ≥ 0. If c(J) ≥ 2, there are positions p ≠ q with J(p) = J(q) = i₀. Then the argument tuple f∘J has equal entries in the distinct slots p and q, so β(f∘J) = 0 because β is alternating (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_eq). Hence c(J)·g(J) = 0 = g(J). Summing over J proves the claim. (This is the parent's restriction to tuples in which i₀ occurs exactly once. Tuples containing i₀ twice contribute 0, and the dropped terms are ≥ 0.)

8. (Total sum.) Σ_{J : Fin (k+1) → Fin N} g(J) = (k+1)!·|β|², by sq_sum applied to the (k+1)-covector β and the orthonormal basis f.

9. (Conclusion.) By steps 5–8, (k+1)·k!·|ι_uβ|² = Σ_{p ∈ Fin (k+1)} R_p ≤ (k+1)!·|β|² = (k+1)·k!·|β|². Divide by (k+1)·k! > 0 to get |ι_uβ|² ≤ |β|². Both norms are ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg), so |ι_uβ| ≤ |β|. With step 3, |ι_vβ| = ‖v‖·|ι_uβ| ≤ ‖v‖·|β|, that is, covectorEuclideanNorm (β.curryLeft v) ≤ ‖v‖ * covectorEuclideanNorm β. ∎
proof_key_steps: Homogeneity |c·γ| = |c|·|γ| and the case v = 0; otherwise reduce to u = v/‖v‖ = f_{i₀} for an orthonormal basis f (Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq).
Position sums R_p := Σ_{J(p) = i₀} β(f∘J)²: R_0 = k!·|ι_uβ|² by Fin.cons reindexing and sq_sum.
R_p = R_0 by the transposition 0 ↔ p (sign² = 1).
Σ_p R_p ≤ Σ_J β(f∘J)² = (k+1)!·|β|², because tuples with i₀ in two slots vanish; cancel (k+1)·k! and take square roots.
